findings.claim: `issue.options` is not a property of the `invalid_union` issue type in Zod v4 (union issues carry `errors`, a nested array of issue arrays; `options` belongs to `invalid_value`/enum-style issues). This guard therefore likely never passes, making the discriminator message — the very string being edited in this diff — dead code.
findings.rationale: If the runtime issue object has no `options`, the reworded branch can never be reached and the locale silently falls through to the generic "Вуруди нодуруст". It also implies an unsafe/implicit access on a union-typed issue. Medium confidence — depends on the exact `$ZodIssueInvalidUnion` shape in this version, but other locales in this package do not key off `issue.options` for `invalid_union`.

findings.claim: `${o}` interpolates each option with default string conversion; non-primitive options (objects, or nested issue arrays if `options` ever is populated) render as `'[object Object]'`.
findings.rationale: Produces a useless user-facing message for any non-string/number option. Other locales typically use `util.joinValues` / `util.stringifyPrimitive` for this reason. Medium-high confidence that raw interpolation is wrong here.

findings.claim: The message is hardcoded to talk about a "discriminator" even though the branch is reached for any `invalid_union` issue, not just discriminated unions.
findings.rationale: A plain (non-discriminated) union failure would produce a message referring to a discriminator that does not exist, which is misleading to end users. The diff rewords this string without addressing the mismatch. Low-medium confidence, since it depends on whether `options` is ever populated for plain unions.
